selection.preview: model_preview true, no packs (103 authored bindings)

method.trials: 3 serial fresh processes per fixture and selection; medians of the three per-trial means
method.ticks: 10 warmup + 60 measured, fixed 1/30 s simulation step
method.quality: requested_msaa 4 / actual_msaa 4, 1280x800 drawable and viewport, requested vsync 0, reported swap interval 0, shader on
method.machine: Apple M4, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, GL 2.1 Metal - 90.5, pygame-ce 2.5.8 / SDL 2.32.10
method.semantics: synchronized diagnostic frame cost with glFinish stage boundaries, NOT interactive FPS
method.harness: tools/acceptance/measure_catalogue_cost.py configures the real selection seam then calls the real benchmark CLI; no product, fixture or quality parameter changed
method.discarded_trials: 2 of the 24 trials were discarded and re-run: the benchmark CLI does not expose --screenshot (it is a run_benchmark() keyword, not a parser argument), so the two preview trials that asked for captures exited 1 with 'unrecognized arguments'. They were re-run with the identical measurement flags and no capture. No preview screenshot is therefore part of this record; the frozen-package capture in artifacts/s09/package/ is a separate --smoke artifact.

trial_count.note: every reported trial is a completed run of the committed harness; the two discarded attempts measured nothing

method.environment: A leaked process tree from the earlier protected single-process suite (protected_suite.py, started 14:04) wrote its result at 14:24 but never exited; it held a live SDL/GL context and averaged ~62% CPU until it was reaped at ~19:5x. Both the per-module gate and this sweep therefore ran beside a competitor, not on an idle machine.
method.contention_check: The legacy medians here (41.97 / 56.87 ms) sit ~8-10% above the post-optimization reference in GRAPHICS_DRAW_SCOPE_REUSE.md (38.84 / 51.22 ms), which is the size of drift mild contention would produce. The authored-vs-legacy ratios (4.5-6.2x) are far larger than that margin, so the verdict is unaffected; the absolute milliseconds should be re-measured on an idle machine before any optimization work is planned against them.

conclusion.performance_reference: NOT MET by either selection on any fixture; the adopted 60 FPS / 30 FPS reference is 5-40x below measured cost
conclusion.catalogue_cost: opting into the 103-binding authored catalogue multiplies frame cost by 4.5x-5.8x (stock 42->188 ms, 57->293 ms; stress 113->705 ms, 353->2034 ms)
conclusion.where_the_cost_is: render-side only: world stage 27.65->245.03 ms and camera 1.60->16.64 ms on stock combat, while simulation (20.79->20.29 ms), HUD (5.38->5.06 ms) and LAN checksum (9.17->8.84 ms) are unchanged
conclusion.determinism: initial and final state hashes and LAN precise checksums are identical between selections on all four fixtures, and stable across all three trials - the catalogue is a view, not simulation state
unverified_hypotheses: the authored hulls carry roughly two orders of magnitude more triangles than the procedural shapes they replace, so display-list replay is vertex-throughput bound rather than call bound
the camera stage growth suggests authored bounds are recomputed per entity from full mesh extents rather than from the cached canonical bounds
conclusion.not_an_optimization_authorization: recording this gap authorizes no renderer change, quality reduction or workload edit; renderer work remains a separate authorized workstream
